questions.text: A system takes source speech from speaker A and a reference voice from speaker B, then produces B’s voice saying the source words. Which task is this?
questions.explanation: Voice conversion preserves the source speech content while changing speaker identity; text-based cloning instead starts with text plus a reference voice.

questions.text: A generated clip has high speaker-embedding similarity to its target voice. What additional check addresses whether it actually says the intended words?

options.A: Measure similarity between two target reference recordings.
options.B: Check only the duration of the generated clip.
options.C: Check whether the watermark payload is recoverable.
options.D: Transcribe the generated clip and compute CER or WER against the intended text.

questions.explanation: Speaker similarity measures voice identity, while ASR-based CER or WER checks intelligibility and content accuracy.

questions.text: The toy gate first asserts verify_signature(record), then asserts record["speaker_id"] == hash_speaker(ref_audio), then calls tts.infer and watermark. With Python assertions enabled, a valid signature, and a mismatched speaker_id, what happens?

options.A: AssertionError is raised before synthesis or watermarking.
options.B: Synthesis runs, but watermarking is skipped.
options.C: Watermarked audio is returned because the signature is valid.
options.D: The speaker_id is automatically replaced before synthesis.

questions.explanation: The second assertion fails and raises AssertionError, so neither the synthesis nor watermark call is reached.
